Labeled defect
- root cause: style() tests fg and bg for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so the 256-color index 0 is skipped
- failure path: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0, meaning black, applies no color at all and the text renders in the terminal default; the caller sees no error

Reviewer finding
- description: Truthiness checks replace `is not None`, so a valid color value of integer 0 (the 256-color palette entry for black) is silently skipped and no color code is emitted.
- rationale: Trigger: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0. `if fg:` is False for 0, so no escape sequence is appended and the text is uncolored, with no error. The same applies to bg at line 684.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: `style()` tests fg/bg by truthiness instead of `is not None`, so integer 0 (256-color black) is skipped. It also gives the same outcome, uncolored text with no error.
